subject.title: [Bug]: OpenClaw leaks unreaped hook/tool child processes, causing zombie accumulation and runtime degradation

question: Should the linked fix be reworked around demonstrated child ownership and wait semantics, or is there evidence that a generic process-wide reaper is required?
rationale: The issue is credible and urgent, but the proposed generic SIGCHLD mechanism does not reproduce the reported kernel state and crosses the gateway-wide process boundary; selecting that architecture requires process-owner judgment and branch-tied Linux proof.

options.title: Require owner-boundary proof
options.body: Rework the fix to identify each leaking spawn path, correct its wait or termination lifecycle, and provide current-main Linux/Docker before-and-after soak evidence.

options.title: Adopt a native reaper design
options.body: Approve a platform-specific subreaper or wait mechanism only after a minimal adopted-grandchild zombie reproducer proves that owner-boundary cleanup cannot cover the observed process classes.

recommendation.title: Require owner-boundary proof
recommendation.body: Rework the fix to identify each leaking spawn path, correct its wait or termination lifecycle, and provide current-main Linux/Docker before-and-after soak evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this contributor most directly to the shared exec and supervisor lifecycle boundaries that must define the repair.
